t: Created by the Congress of Vienna in 1815 and ruled by the Dutch kings until 1890, it lost its western half to Belgium in 1839.
Iron ore and steel, then banking and investment funds, made a poor farming country one of the richest in the world per head.
Occupied by Germany in both world wars, it abandoned neutrality and became a founding member and seat of European institutions.
dyk: The Schengen Agreement that abolished border checks across much of Europe is named after a small wine-growing village in Luxembourg, where it was signed on a boat on the Moselle in 1985.
ev: The Congress of Vienna creates the grand duchy under William I of the Netherlands
The Treaty of London gives the western, French-speaking half to Belgium
The Treaty of London declares Luxembourg neutral and orders its fortress demolished
Adolphe of Nassau-Weilburg becomes grand duke, ending the union with the Netherlands
Germany invades; Grand Duchess Charlotte and the government go into exile
The High Authority of the European Coal and Steel Community settles in Luxembourg
The Schengen Agreement is signed at the village of Schengen

f.founder: Congress of Vienna; William I of the Netherlands (first grand duke)
f.predecessor: Duchy of Luxembourg; French Département des Forêts
